title: Fast in vitro protocol for the visualization and quantitative high-throughput analysis of sprouting angiogenesis by confocal microscopy
protocol: Thaw 1 vial of HUVECs and seed into a gelatin-coated T75.
Replate HUVECs into appropriate number of coated T150s after 1 or 2 days, usually 3–4 plates.
Seed HUVECs for lentiviral transduction into coated 6-well plates at 40%–60% confluency, 1 or 2 wells per condition.
Transduce HUVECs with virus-like particles the following day.
Incubate HUVECs for 12–16 hours with shRNA lentivirus solution (1 mL/well) in DMEM supplemented with EGM-2.
Mix EGM-2 with puromycin at a concentration of 1 μg/mL.
Replace the medium with the EGM-2-puromycin solution to select for positive cells.
Work in the flow hood to keep cells and materials sterile.
Transfer 250 μl of resuspended beads to a sterile 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube.
Allow beads to settle and remove supernatant.
Add 250 μl of EGM-2.
Harvest HUVECs by trypsinization and resuspend in EGM-2.
Count cells using a cell counter.
Adjust cells to a concentration of 660,000 cells/ml.
Attach cells to beads by adding 1.5 ml of cell suspension to a 50 ml tube.
Resuspend beads and add 40 μl to the cell suspension.
Place cell/bead mixture at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 4 h.
Resuspend every 20 min.
Incubate cell/bead mixture with T25 by adding 3.5 ml of EGM-2 to T25.
Allow incubation at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 12–16 h.
Harvest HUVEC-coated beads by resuspending them and transferring to a 50 ml tube.
Rinse T25 once with 3 ml of EGM-2 and add to the same tube.
Visually inspect HUVEC adhesion efficiency to Cytodex beads.
Wash HUVEC-coated beads by removing supernatant, adding 1 mL of EGM-2, resuspending, and allowing the beads to settle. Repeat as necessary.
Add 0.6 ml of 10 mg/ml fibrinogen to 2.4 ml of PBS, then add 18 μL of 15 U/mL aprotinin.
Remove supernatant from beads and add fibrinogen/aprotinin/PBS mixture to the 50 mL tube.
Pipette a drop of 1,875 μl of a 10 U/ml thrombin solution in the middle of a well on a glass-bottom 96 well plate.
Add 30 μL of the fibrinogen/aprotinin/PBS mixture containing HUVEC-coated beads and resuspend gently.
Allow the fibrin gel to polymerize for 5 min in the flow hood at 20°C–22°C.
Gently place plate in incubator for 15 min.
Very gently drip 100 μL of EGM-2 on top of the gel.
Place HUVEC/bead/gel mixture at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 20–48 h.
Aspirate the medium.
Wash once with PBS containing MgCl2/CaCl2.
Fix with 500 μL of 4% PFA for 15 min at 20°C–22°C.
Wash with PBS.
Permeabilize with 500 μL of 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Block non-specific binding with 5% BSA in PBS containing MgCl2/CaCl2 for 2 hours at 20°C–22°C.
Wash the gels three times with PBS containing MgCl2/CaCl2.
Incubate with Hoechst and phalloidin for 12 to 16 hours at 4°C.
Wash gels three times with PBS containing MgCl2/CaCl2 for 10 minutes.
Store gels at 4°C until imaging.
Apply two drops of water to the lens of a 20× long-distance water objective.
Place a drop of water on the bottom of the 96-well plate underneath the wells to be filmed.
Place the plate on the stage of a confocal microscope.
Select objectives with long working distance for imaging.
Prefer water objectives over oil-immersion objectives.
Use a water pump to maintain water immersion during longer imaging periods.
Limit magnification to 20–25× when imaging entire beads and sprouts.
Choose appropriate laser lines: excitation at 405 nm for Hoechst, and 561/594 nm for Texas Red-conjugated phalloidin.

Determine laser/gain and other confocal settings such as image dimensions of 1024 × 1024 pixels, 0.75 μm/pixel, pinhole 1 μm, scan speed 400 Hz, bidirectional scanning, and sequential scanning between stacks.
Optimize laser and gain settings.
Set the appropriate number of z-slices.
Run a pilot stack to confirm or adjust settings.
Select xyz positions and save to positions list.
Start the experiment.
Create the positions list at the end of the day for the confocal run to last 12-16 hours.
Reduce scanning time to about 3 minutes per bead using resonant scanning for imaging large numbers of beads.
Image multiple beads (5-10) per condition to account for bead-to-bead heterogeneity and variability in sprouting.
Select beads for imaging in a blind manner to reduce potential bias.
Use microscope applications such as Leica Navigator to scan the entire well at low magnification for unbiased bead selection.
Acquire phase/contrast images of the same plate in parallel to confirm differences in sprouting between conditions.
Trypsinize HUVECs of experimental condition and control.
Count HUVECs and resuspend equal numbers in EGM-2.
Add CellTracker Green dye to the experimental condition HUVECs at a concentration of 0.1 μM.
Add CellTracker Red dye to the control HUVECs at a concentration of 0.1 μM.
Wash cells twice with large volumes of PBS.
Pre-incubate HUVECs in the dark at 37°C for 30 min.
Mix two populations of labeled HUVECs in a 1:1 ratio.
Incubate the mixture with beads at 37°C for 12–16 h.
Harvest beads with labeled HUVECs as described in steps 13 and 14.
Add beads with labeled HUVECs to fibrin gels.
Start sprouting assay as described in steps 15–17.
Fix cells at an appropriate time-point, such as 20 hours after the induction of sprouting.
Determine cellular health by visual inspection.
Label fixed cells with Hoechst.
Keep plates in the dark to avoid loss of CellTracker signal.
Select the appropriate laser lines on a confocal set-up (e.g., 405 nm for Hoechst, 488 nm for CellTracker Green, and 591 nm for CellTracker Red).
Image the cells as described above.
Create maximum projections of the z-stacks.
Quantify tip cells by counting all tip cells for each color.
Divide this number by the total number of cells in that color to correct for potential differences in total cell numbers in each condition.
Determine the best conditions for labeling with CellTracker dyes.
Include a condition where different CellTracker dyes are swapped between cell populations.
Include a condition where control cells labeled with either dye are mixed in a 1:1 ratio.
Perform live imaging by time-lapse confocal microscopy.
Label endothelial cells using CellTracker dyes as described above.
Or: Follow steps 22–32 to produce lentivirus-like particles, using the lentiviral expression vector of interest.
Transduce HUVECs following steps 1–5 for endothelial cell culture and lentiviral transduction.
Select positive cells with antibiotics as described in step 6 of section “Endothelial cell culture and lentiviral transduction”.
Transduce HUVECs with lentiviral vector containing the fluorescent protein of interest.
Select stable knockdown cells first, followed by transduction to express the marker protein if necessary.
Attach the fluorescent HUVECs to beads as described in step 21.
Determine the best time-point to start imaging.
Replace the medium approximately 1 hour before setting up the microscope.
Prewarm and stabilize the microscope at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Select the appropriate laser lines and settings for imaging.
Determine the optimal confocal settings, including number of z-slices per position and intervals between images.
Assess potential phototoxicity and bleaching effects before starting the experiment.
Start the experiment as described in step 19.
